paragraphs.text: # Greece Travel Guide: Where to Go, What to Do, Eat & Stay

Greece remains one of the most photographed destinations in the world for good reason — whitewashed buildings, blue domes, and some of the clearest water in the Mediterranean. Whether you're chasing sunsets in Santorini or history in Athens, here's everything you need to plan the trip.
## Getting There

Direct flights from most UK airports run around 3.5–4 hours in peak season. From the US, most routes connect through a European hub (London, Frankfurt, or Amsterdam are common layovers), with total travel time typically 11–14 hours depending on connections. Athens International Airport (ATH) is the main gateway; from there, domestic flights or ferries connect to the islands.
## Where to Stay

- **Santorini** — Caldera-view hotels in Oia and Fira book out fast in summer; reserve 4–6 months ahead for peak season (June–August). Expect premium pricing for the classic cave-hotel-with-a-view experience.
- **Athens** — Offers far more budget flexibility as a base. The Plaka and Koukaki neighborhoods put you walking distance from the Acropolis with a wide range of hotel prices.
- **Mykonos** — Split between the lively main town (Chora) for nightlife and quieter areas like Agios Ioannis for a calmer stay.
- **Crete** — A good value alternative to the Cyclades, with more affordable stays and a mix of beach resorts and mountain villages.
## What to Do
- Watch the sunset in **Oia, Santorini** — arrive early to claim a good viewing spot, as it gets crowded.
- Explore the **Acropolis and Ancient Agora** in Athens; go early morning to beat the heat and crowds.
- Island-hop by ferry between **Mykonos, Paros, and Naxos** for a mix of beach clubs and quieter villages.
- Visit **Knossos Palace** in Crete for Minoan history.
- Take a boat tour around Santorini's caldera, including a stop at the volcanic hot springs.
## What to Eat
Greek food is built around fresh, simple ingredients. Don't miss:
- **Souvlaki and gyros** from casual street-side spots — some of the best meals in Greece cost only a few euros.
- **Fresh seafood** at tavernas right on the water, especially grilled octopus and whole fish.
- **Greek salad (horiatiki)** made with tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and feta — simpler and better than most versions abroad.
- **Moussaka** and other baked dishes for a heartier meal.
- Local wine from Santorini, which has a unique volcanic-soil character (try Assyrtiko).
## Practical Tips
- Peak season (July–August) is hot, crowded, and expensive; late May, June, and September offer better weather-to-crowd ratios.
- Ferries between islands can be delayed or cancelled due to wind — build buffer days into your itinerary if island-hopping.
- Cobbled and stepped streets are common, especially in Santorini — comfortable shoes matter more than style here.
- Many smaller tavernas and shops are cash-preferred, though cards are increasingly accepted.
Greece rewards travelers who mix at least one island with a couple of days in Athens — the contrast between ancient history and laid-back island life is part of what makes the country so memorable.
